source_text.body:
Hand off messy file-based tasks with a defined "done"
A commenter gives Claude files plus a description of done; others mention it organizing desktop folders and doing repetitive office work.
·
Sep 1, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
One commenter stopped treating Claude like search and started handing it whole file-based jobs with messy inputs plus a clear description of what finished output should look like. In the thread, people describe giving it folders, exports, sheets, or existing data connections and having it handle the intermediate steps, while they still reviewed the final numbers or output before using it.
How it went
The thread reports it could return work people would actually ship, organize repetitive reporting, and even shrink one manual file-posting workflow from 20 minutes to 10 seconds and two clicks. The common limit was that users still checked results, especially final numbers or documents.
Worth knowing
The main catch is that it works best when you define “done” clearly and hand over the full messy context instead of asking for little answers.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
Work in my folder [folder path]. Here is the task: [describe task, e.g., sort files into folders by project and rename them consistently, or pull figures from these files into one sheet]. Done means [clear finish condition, e.g., no loose files left, every file named YYYY-MM-DD-description]. Before moving, renaming, or deleting anything, show me the plan and wait for my approval, and never delete anything permanently.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1w0k45r/what_task_did_you_stop_doing_yourself_once_this
